articles.title: Elton John, Oprah Winfrey, Sabrina Carpenter and Paul McCartney offer Dolly Parton tributes
articles.summary: The tributes have included artists across musical genres, fans from all generations and politicians from all spectrum sharing their love for the country icon.
articles.body:
Sir Paul McCartney, Oprah Winfrey and Sir Elton John have led a wave of personal tributes to music icon Dolly Parton, honouring her impact across the globe.

The Beatles legend called Parton a "magnificent star", Oprah said she "brought the light" and the Rocket Man singer dubbed her a "giant of an artist" who was "irreplaceable".

Parton died on Tuesday at the age of 80, following health issues that caused the cancellation of her Las Vegas residency earlier this year.

Tributes have poured in from US presidents across the political spectrum and musicians across all genres, remembering her not just for her award-winning career, but her philanthropy and humble nature that transcended country music.

McCartney reflected on his history with Parton, which began when he met her in Nashville at the Grande Ole Opry right before starting her solo musical career.

"She was so bubbly and full of life, it is difficult to take in the news that she has passed," he said. "Her songwriting, her singing and her philanthropy were unrivaled in the world of country music and it is hard to imagine living in a world without Dolly."

John said he was "shocked and devastated" over the news. "A giant of an artist - unique and irreplaceable, with the kindest heart".

Former talk-show host Winfrey wrote that one of her fondest memories with Parton was "having a hoot and a holler while wearing Bob Mackie gowns on her show Dolly".

"This girl from the Smoky Mountains of Tennessee dreamed a life and then lived a life bigger than she could have ever imagined, giving so generously to others in ways we saw and ways we didn't."

Parton's musical influence spanned generations, even inspiring the careers of a younger wave of female talent, including pop stars Sabrina Carpenter and Miley Cyrus.

The pair collaborated in 2025 for a country-inspired remix and music video of Carpenter's hit song Please Please Please.

"The only thing I could say after we first met was 'she really is an angel walking the earth' and 'we look like we could be sisters!'" Carpenter wrote on Instagram.

Along with behind the scenes pictures of the pair filming their music video, Carpenter added: "Your light will be something the world will search forever to find again."

Singer Miley Cyrus is Parton's goddaughter. The pair teamed up on a new version of Cyrus's 2013 song Wrecking Ball â and Parton appeared on several episodes of Hannah Montana, in which Cyrus starred.

Cyrus's father and Parton's close friend Billy Ray Cyrus remembered the music icon as being "part of our lives, on our TV's, right in our living rooms".

"I have so many moments and memories with Dolly, it's hard to know where to start," Billy Ray Cyrus said. "Like every little boy, I grew up loving Dolly Parton."

He recounted a time when he had to apologise to Parton for tabloid rumours which claimed he was having an affair with her.

"In true Dolly fashion, she just looked at me, winked and said: "Honey, this trash sells records!"

The wave of musical talents honouring Parton has stretched from fellow country star Reba McEntire to rapper Eminem, with each sharing personal stories on how important the late singer was to them and the world as a whole.

McEntire thanked Parton for "all the wonderful things you did for us here on earth. "Your love, your music and you gave so much with your huge huge heart. There will never ever be another you".

"We will remember and cherish every memory and every note you ever played and sang," McEntire wrote. "Thank you, Lord, for Dolly. She's gonna have a blast in heaven singing all her favorite songs with all her family and friends who have gone on before her."

Rapper Eminem noted that even while he had never met Parton, she still made her mark on his life with a note she sent calling him "very special".

"I'm sorry we never got a chance to meet, but getting this note from Dolly really had a an impact on me. She definitely didn't have to take the time to do it," he said, posting a photo of a letter from her congratulating him on his induction in the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame.

articles.title: Port Houston donates $500,000 to 32 nonprofits, supporting workforce training, STEM education and community projects
articles.summary: US News: Port Houston has awarded $500,000 in Community Grants to 32 organisations serving communities across the Houston Ship Channel region. The funding will.
articles.body: Port Houston has awarded $500,000 in Community Grants to 32 organisations serving communities across the Houston Ship Channel region. The funding will support programmes ranging from workforce training and STEM education to healthcare access, food assistance, environmental projects and neighbourhood improvements. According to Port Houston press release distributed via Business Wire, the latest grant cycle attracted 194 applications requesting more than $6.6 million, highlighting the scale of demand for community investment. Nearly half of the funding awarded this year is dedicated to workforce development, with supported programmes helping students explore career paths, earn industry-recognised credentials and develop skills for maritime, logistics and industrial careers. Since launching the Community Grants Programme in 2020, Port Houston has invested more than $2.15 million in local organisations. The 2026 awards also mark a transition, with future grants from 2027 set to follow priorities identified through Port Houstonâs Anchored in Action Community Investment Plan.32 organisations receive funding for education, health, food and environmental projectsThe 32 grant recipients represent a broad cross-section of community initiatives. Armand Bayou Nature Center received $15,000 for school field-trip access, while the Barbara Bush Houston Literacy Foundation received $25,000 for East End community STEM literacy initiatives. Baytown Habitat for Humanity was awarded $15,000 for its Safe and Stable Homes Repair & Resilience Initiative, and Art League of Baytown received $7,250 for its Arts and the Ship Channel programme. Compudopt received $25,000 for its Pathways Programme, while Galena Park Resource and Training Center was awarded $25,000 for community learning and engagement. Lee College Foundation received $20,000 for logistics software expansion, linking education directly to one of the regionâs major employment sectors. The grants also address health, food security and access to essential services. articles.title: Mumbai auto drivers learn to refuse rides... in Marathi
articles.summary: MUMBAI: 'No' has got some stiff competition in Mumbai after the mandatory requirement of working knowledge of Marathi has, of late, seen cab and autor.
articles.body: MUMBAI: 'No' has got some stiff competition in Mumbai after the mandatory requirement of working knowledge of Marathi has, of late, seen cab and autorickshaw drivers rushing to polish their language skills. After having picked up basic Marathi at RTO-run language classes, some auto drivers are using their newly acquired vocabulary to rustle up a string of excuses to refuse rides.One auto driver in Kurla has scribbled down what he claims are essential phrases in Marathi to get by. Most of these are different ways to turn down passengers - from "mala jevayla jayche aahe" (I need to eat), "mala lagvi la jayche aahe" (I need to use the restroom) and "mala ghari jaychay" (I need to go home), to "mala gas bharaychay" (I need to refill CNG) and "mala riksha durust karaychi aahe" (I need to repair the auto).The driver's notes aren't entirely dedicated to strategic refusals, though. They include practical phrases such as "hoy, basa" (yes, please sit), "kuthey jaychay?" (where do you want to go?), "to kuthe aahe?" (where is that place?) and "ujvi/davi kade gheu?" (should I take a right/left?). Along with the all-important financial vocabulary of Mumbai's transport ecosystem: "sutte dya" (please give change) and "sutte nahi" (I don't have change).The rush for acquiring Marathi-speaking skills comes as the state has enforced the amended Motor Vehicles Rules that require drivers of all commercial passenger vehicles in the state to possess a working knowledge of the language.However, the fear of a crackdown saw a large-scale protest by a section of non-Marathi-speaking autorickshaw and taxi drivers, who stayed off the roads Monday. As commuters bore the brunt, facing travel disruptions and steep fare hikes, state govt Tuesday sought to reassure transport workers by announcing 161 Marathi language training centres across the state and a dedicated RTO helpline to address complaints of harassment, illegal fines and alleged irregularities during Marathi proficiency checks. Transport minister Pratap Sarnaik said the centres would become operational within the next two to three days.Drivers who fail the on-road tests for Marathi-speaking skills are being given a one-month notice period to learn the language. However, driver unions have sought more time and support for compliance. CM Devendra Fadnavis had said Monday that govt was willing to give more time to learn the language.Sarnaik clarified that drivers would first receive a one-month notice, followed by a three-month suspension period. During this time, no immediate licence cancellation would take place, he said.For Mumbai's passengers, however, the real test of auto drivers' Marathi proficiency may be when "hoy, basa" becomes more common than "mala ghari jaychay".You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.summary: VIJAYAWADA: Six people, including five women, were killed and at least 12 others injured after a private bus carrying 42 passengers rammed into a truc.
articles.body: VIJAYAWADA: Six people, including five women, were killed and at least 12 others injured after a private bus carrying 42 passengers rammed into a truck in Telanganaâs Suryapet district early Wednesday, police said.The accident occurred around 4.30am near Kodad mandal when the bus, travelling from Hyderabad to Eluru in Andhra Pradesh, hit the truck from behind, according to preliminary investigations.A senior police official said six people died in the accident, while the injured were shifted to a hospital for treatment.Police suspect the truck had first hit a road divider before the bus crashed into it.Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy expressed condolences over the deaths and conveyed his sympathies to the bereaved families.The chief minister also directed the chief secretary to take necessary steps to ensure advanced medical treatment for those injured in the accident, an official release said.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. articles.title: US Court to pharma giant Guardant Health: You willfully infringed patents for cancer-testing; asked to pay $245 million to University of Washington
articles.summary: Tech News News: A federal judge has finalized a judgment ordering pharma giant Guardant Health to pay more than $245 million to Seattle-based biotech startup TwinStra.
articles.body: A federal judge has finalized a judgment ordering pharma giant Guardant Health to pay more than $245 million to Seattle-based biotech startup TwinStrand Biosciences and the University of Washington for willfully infringing on patented DNA sequencing technology. The final order, entered in the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware, formalizes an initial November 2023 jury verdict against Guardant. In addition to the upfront payout, the ruling guarantees TwinStrand and the university an ongoing 6% royalty on covered Guardant products through the expiration of the patents in March 2033.TwinStrand was spun out of the University of Washington in 2015 to commercialize the platform. Among its co-founders is molecular biologist and oncologist Dr Jesse Salkâgrandson of polio vaccine developer Jonas Salkâwho served as CEO until 2022 and now co-leads cancer diagnostics firm CytoTerra. Since its founding, TwinStrand has drawn backing from prominent venture firms, including Madrona Venture Group, Soleus Capital, and Section 32, the latter of which led a $50 million Series B round in 2021.The dispute centers on 'Duplex Sequencing,' a breakthrough method developed at the University of Washington that increases the accuracy of next-generation DNA sequencing by more than 10,000-fold. By eliminating standard sequencing errors, the technology allows clinicians and researchers to detect ultra-rare genetic mutations critical for early cancer detection and monitoring.The jury found that Guardant incorporated this proprietary technology without a license across 11 diagnostic products and services, including its flagship Guardant360, Guardant Reveal, and Guardant Shield tests. Following the verdict, the Delaware court denied Guardant's motions to overturn the decision or grant a new trial."Duplex Sequencing solved an accuracy problem the sequencing field had worked on for years, and this judgment affirms the juryâs finding that Guardant Health built products on that invention without a license," said Chad Waite, chair of TwinStrandâs board of directors. "We remained steadfast in our conviction that the facts would prevail, and they have."The $245.2 million total includes: $83.4 million in original jury-awarded damages for infringement through June 2023; $119.4 million in accrued royalties; $22.9 million in interest; and $19.5 million in supplemental damages.Guardant Health says that it will appealGuardant Health announced that it will appeal the final judgment from the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware related to intellectual property claims brought against Guardant by TwinStrand Biosciences, Inc. and University of Washington, with execution of the final judgment and collection of potential royalties stayed pending appeal.âWe strongly disagree with this decision and will promptly be appealing for its overturn,â said John Saia, Guardant Health Chief Legal Officer. âWe have full faith in the strengths and merits of Guardantâs intellectual property and R&D and are confident we will ultimately prevail on appeal.âImportantly, the order published regarding the scope of royalties expressly defined the products included as those that existed at the time of the trial in 2023, many of which have been discontinued or significantly upgraded. Based on Guardantâs updated technology the current versions of Guardant Reveal and Shield are excluded from the order and potential royalties. In addition, the company has validated design improvements to Guardant360 and related services that would exclude impact of the potential ongoing royalties in the decision.Guardant remains confident that it did not infringe the asserted patents. Both TwinStrand patents have been preliminarily invalidated in the companyâs ongoing challenges before the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office. Separately, Guardant is pursuing appeals before the US Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit.Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: âThey opposed Ambedkarâs Constitution, wanted Manusmritiâ: Owaisi targets RSS, BJP
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi has launched a sharp attack on the RSS and BJP over the Manusmriti, questioning their commitment to the In.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi has launched a sharp attack on the RSS and BJP over the Manusmriti, questioning their commitment to the Indian Constitution. He accused them of historically favouring the ancient text over the document adopted by the country.Owaisi made the remarks during his address at the Jalsa-e-Rahmatul-lil-Alameen at Darussalam .n Hyderabad on the occasion of the 1501st Eid Milad-un-Nabi. He targeted the RSS over its reported opposition to the Constitution drafted by Dr BR Ambedkar and contrasted the organisation's position with that of Muslim freedom fighters during British rule."I am asking those associated with the RSS about Manusmriti. Is it not true that on November 26, 1949, we adopted the Constitution? Yet, four days later, on November 30, a mouthpiece of the RSS published a complaint against it, stating that it wasn't a constitution at all and that it should have been the Manusmriti. They had issues with the Constitution drafted by Babasaheb Ambedkar," Owaisi said.The AIMIM chief also attacked Hindutva ideologue VD Savarkar, referring to his correspondence with the British during his imprisonment in the Andaman cellular jail."Savarkar was in support of Manusmriti. While he was in Andaman jail, he was writing letters to the British, saying, 'I am with you, please release me.' But what were we doing? Allama Fazl-e-Haq Khairabadi was also in jail; he endured hardships but never wrote a 'love letter' to the British. Instead, he issued a fatwa for Jihad against them. Even today, his grave stands in the Andaman as a testament," he asserted.Owaisi further sought to highlight the role of Muslim figures in India's freedom struggle. He claimed that the first prisoner sent to the Andaman Islands was Maulvi Alauddin, the Imam of Hyderabad's Mecca Masjid."Listen, BJP and RSS people, who was the first prisoner in Andaman? It was not your father, grandfather, or ancestor. It was Hyderabad's Maulvi Alauddin, the Imam of Mecca Masjid. He was the first prisoner," Owaisi told the gathering.His remarks come amid an intensifying political confrontation between the BJP and Congress over the Manusmriti and its place in India's social and constitutional discourse.The BJP has recently targeted Congress leader and Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi over his criticism of the Manusmriti. It accused Rahul of making statements that undermine India's traditions, cultural heritage and democratic institutions. Several BJP leaders, including chief ministers, have alleged that Rahul Gandhi's remarks sought to "belittle" India's civilisational values.At an event titled 'Chhatron ki Goonj' in Pune, Rahul Gandhi criticised a passage attributed to the Manusmriti concerning women's independence."This is a direct quote from the Manusmriti, and these words are a shame, because these words should never ever have been spoken," Gandhi said after quoting the passage: "In childhood, a female belongs to her father. In youth, she belongs to her husband. When her lord is dead, she belongs to her sons. A woman must never be independent."Rahul also called for an end to patriarchal structures, telling female students that the country needs to "smash the prevailing patriarchy" to achieve genuine empowerment for women.The exchange has brought the Manusmriti back into the centre of a wider political debate over constitutional values, social equality and competing interpretations of India's cultural and political history.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: US halts visa appointments globally amid Donald Trump's immigration crackdown
articles.summary: US News: The US has paused visa appointments for applicants around the world as the Trump administration launches a global training programme for consular offi.
articles.body: The US has paused visa appointments for applicants around the world as the Trump administration launches a global training programme for consular officers amid its broader immigration crackdown.A US State Department spokesperson said on Tuesday that the department had begun a training initiative at all US embassies and consulates worldwide. Visa appointment schedules will be adjusted to accommodate the training, the spokesperson said, according to Reuters.The State Department did not provide details on the training or specify how long the adjustments would last.It said the programme was aimed at helping consular officers screen applicants who could potentially become dependent on US public benefits and ensure that visa applications are evaluated "comprehensively and consistently".According to a Financial Times report, immigrant visa applicants with scheduled interviews at US embassies and consulates had received emails informing them that their appointments were being rescheduled and that they would be notified of new dates.The development comes as President Donald Trump's administration continues a broad immigration crackdown that has included visa and green-card revocations and the rejection of applications on various grounds, including political opinions and participation in pro-Palestinian protests.Trump has said the crackdown is intended to improve domestic security.Immigration crackdown faces legal challengesThe administration's immigration policies have also faced legal setbacks. A US judge on Friday struck down a policy that suspended the issuance of immigrant visas to applicants from 75 countries, ruling that the measure exceeded secretary of state Marco Rubio's statutory authority.The administration has also moved to tighten restrictions on legal immigration.The US Department of Homeland Security has proposed making permanent a $103,265 fee for new cap-subject H-1B visa petitions, after a previous $100,000 fee imposed by Trump was blocked by a court.The proposed fee would significantly increase the cost for employers hiring foreign workers in specialised fields.The H-1B programme allows US employers to hire foreign workers with specialised training. The programme provides 65,000 visas annually, along with another 20,000 for workers with advanced degrees.Trump's administration has also ordered enhanced vetting of H-1B applicants and proposed changes to the visa selection process that would favour higher-skilled and better-paid workers.Visa revocations add to pressure on applicantsThe administration is separately preparing to revoke the business and tourism visas of potentially up to 200,000 foreigners who have applied for or are currently seeking asylum in the US.The proposed action would cover B1 and B2 visas issued between 2016 and 2026 whose holders have sought or are seeking asylum. The State Department is expected to announce the move in the coming weeks, according to news agency AP.B1 visas are generally issued for business travel, while B2 visas are generally used for tourism, family visits or medical treatment.The administration has also tightened screening requirements for visa applicants, including demands for additional information about their social media histories and, in some cases, expensive visa bonds.The latest pause in appointments therefore comes as the Trump administration continues to review and tighten several aspects of the US immigration and visa system.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Gao Zhen: China jails artist over satirical Mao Zedong sculptures, say rights groups
articles.summary: The case against Gao Zhen, who was prosecuted under a law banning "slander of heroes", has been seen as an assault on artistic freedom.
articles.body:
A Chinese artist known for his satirical sculptures of Mao Zedong has been handed a maximum three-year jail term for "slandering China's heroes", according to rights groups.

A court in Hebei province had ruled on Tuesday that Gao Zhen's work "infringes upon the hero's reputation and harms public interest".

Among the 70-year-old's most famous pieces, produced with his brother Gao Qiang, is a sculpture comprising a squad of Mao-like figures holding Jesus Christ at gunpoint.

Gao has been in detention for the past two years, and the UN and many rights groups have called for him to be released. Amnesty International has called his sentencing an "assault" on artistic freedom.

Gao had moved to the US in 2022 but was arrested at his studio on the outskirts of Beijing during a visit in August 2024.

Authorities seized his artworks and barred his wife and seven-year-old son from leaving China.

China watchers have said that Gao Zhen's arrest shows how the Chinese Communist Party is becoming increasingly extreme in both grasp and reach – including by policing its citizens transnationally and retroactively.

He was charged under a law that came into force in March 2018, which bans the defamation of historical figures associated with the party.

The Gao brothers' Execution of Christ sculpture was exhibited in 2009, as were two other sculptures cited in the case.

They are Mao's Guilt, a life-sized replica of the leader kneeling in a pose of solemn contrition; and Miss Mao which depicts him with large breasts and a long, Pinocchio-style nose.

Gao's case was heard in a one-day, closed-door trial earlier this year, which received limited coverage in China.

He plans to appeal the conviction, Amnesty International said on Tuesday.

If the verdict is upheld, Gao would be due to complete his sentence in August 2027 as it would take into account the two years that he has already spent in detention.

"No artist should face criminal punishment for creating work that challenges official narratives or encourages critical reflection on history," Amnesty International's China Director Sarah Brooks said on Tuesday.

"This trial demonstrates how broadly worded and politically motivated laws are used – and worse, in this case, used retroactively – to silence artists, activists and other individuals who dare to express views that differ from those of the Chinese government," she said.

"The case against [Gao Zhen] raises particular concerns with regard to the retroactive application of criminal law, the use of criminal sanctions to punish artistic expression, and the impact on his family," the UN's Human Rights Office told AFP news agency.

Earlier this year, his brother Gao Qiang told the BBC that the trial's "message is clear".

"Even if a work was made 15 years ago, it can still be turned into a crime if today's political climate changes," he said.

Art on trial - a sculptor's arrest highlights new extremes for censorship in China
